textbookText: Charles Darwin (1809-1882), a renowned English naturalist, left an indelible mark on the scientific world through his pioneering theory of evolution by natural selection. His groundbreaking book, "On the Origin of Species" (1859), revolutionized biology by proposing that species adapt and evolve over time, driven by natural selection favoring advantageous traits. Additionally, his publication "The Descent of Man" (1871) extended these ideas to human evolution, solidifying his contributions as a cornerstone of modern biology.
